title: Azerbaijani — English/passport-style ASCII (Resolution 498 letter rules)
authority: Letter rules of Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 498 of 16 Dec 2020, Schedule 2 (Azerbaijani→English, geographic names); passport use inferred
description: Azerbaijani Latin to the English spelling used for Azerbaijani names abroad: Ə→A, X→KH, Q→G, Ğ→GH, C→J, Ç→CH, Ş→SH, J→ZH, Ö→O, Ü→U, I/ı→I (Məmmədov → Mammadov, Orxan → Orkhan, Ceyhun → Jeyhun). The letter values are the official ones for geographic names; the only passport evidence is a specimen reading HUSEYNLI ORKHAN.
notes: Resolution 498 Schedule 2 (official, geographic names): a e i o u unchanged; ı→i, ö→o, ü→u; c→j; ç ğ x j ş → ch gh kh zh sh; g and q → g; ə→e in the words Azər, bəy, bəyim, dərə, dəhnə, ət, kənd, köhnə, pəyə, təpə, təzə, otherwise ə→a. Only the exceptions that occur in personal names (Azər, bəy/bəyim) are implemented; traditional exceptions (Bakı→Baku, Azərbaycan→Azerbaijan) are not.

Passport evidence is thin: one PRADO specimen (AZE-AO-02002) seen only as a search snippet shows HUSEYNLI ORKHAN (Ü→U, X→KH). No State Migration Service / MIA transliteration table was found, so Q→G, Ç→CH, Ş→SH, C→J and Ə→A in the MRZ are unverified, though they match the official English forms of public figures (Aliyev, Jeyhun Bayramov, Gurbanov, Shahin Mustafayev).

Alternatives to generate for matching: Ə→E next to l, m, n, r, y (ICT Baku 2023 rule: Azer, Adigozel), Ə→Ä (PCGN substitute, also accepted as input here); Q→Q or K; Ğ→G; X→X or H; J→J; strict ICAO folding (Ç→C, Ş→S, Ğ→G, X and Q kept); Russified forms (Mamedov, Guliyev, Gasanov, Dzhafarov).
Patronymic particles oğlu / qızı become oghlu / gizi here; Russian-document forms are ogly / kyzy.
Cyrillic ә (U+04D9) typed instead of Latin ə (U+0259) is accepted.

rules.note: Resolution 498 §2.4.1: bəy, bəyim → bey, beyim (Ağabəyli → Aghabeyli)
